risk_reasons: A statutory opt-out redemption must preserve its claim-first transaction semantics under concurrent requests.
The transaction boundary controls row-lock scope and PostgreSQL isolation behavior on a public compliance path.
goal: Ensure each Unsubscribe redemption uses a module-owned plain transaction so callers cannot select an unsafe isolation level or extend the token row lock around remote work.
non_goals: Change the four existing redemption outcomes or their HTTP mappings.
Change token admission, receipt, suppression, correction, or single-flight semantics beyond using the new redemption interface.
Add a migration, dependency, deployment, or remote database action.
user_visible_behavior: Concurrent and replayed valid unsubscribe requests retain their current redemption outcomes while the module guarantees a plain transaction boundary.
invariants: Claim the unsubscribe token before recording suppression, using only provenance returned by that claim.
A redeemed token returns a domain outcome rather than exposing a caller-selected transaction isolation failure.
No receipt or success response is emitted before the redemption transaction commits.
The domain module receives its Sql client explicitly and never imports the database singleton.
Raw unsubscribe tokens are not persisted or logged.
edge_cases: A forged token returns unknown_token without opening a transaction.
Overlapping valid redemptions block then resolve as redeemed and already_suppressed without duplicate suppression rows.
A token minted after the claim snapshot remains unknown_token and can be retried.
A purge that commits before a blocked redemption leaves null provenance on the resulting suppression.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/solicitation/unsubscribe.ts redeemUnsubscribeToken claim-first ordering and explicit Sql injection.
src/app/api/u/[token]/route.ts receipt minting after redemption resolves.
tests_to_add: redeemUnsubscribeToken opens its own transaction only after the token admission gate passes
two overlapping redemptions write exactly one ledger row and one redeemed_at
POST mints a receipt only after module-owned redemption commits
single-flight redemption shares the module-owned committed outcome
rollback_plan: Revert the feature commit to restore the prior caller-owned transaction wrapper; no schema or persisted-data rollback is required.
observability: The existing ingress outcome telemetry continues to distinguish redeem failures from committed outcomes, while tests prove the single-flight promise resolves only after the module-owned transaction commits.
